scope: Windows/gfx1151 text AR quantization-drift diagnostics for local Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B Q4 and Q5 against same-conversion-family BF16. Not a replacement complete qualification campaign.
conclusion: Large Q5 distribution shifts persist in an independent engine. Q5 has smaller aggregate KL/TV and sample perplexity loss than the local Q4 control, but a larger maximum TV. Backend/schedule effects also exist; a defective artifact or Gufo kernel bug is not established by the failed pilot cutoff. No additional production change is proposed from this investigation.

sampling_plan.purpose: Attribute Q5 max-row TV failure without changing the original declaration or treating diagnostic calibration as qualification.
sampling_plan.selection: Original leading window plus the next top-level WikiText article heading at/after 20%,40%,60%,80% of source character length. First 513 tokens per sample, 512 next-token labels; no cherry-picking by metrics.
sampling_plan.reference_diagnostics: Compare independent llama.cpp BF16 at the original worst history; subsequently check the worst Q5 row from each window on llama.cpp BF16 and Q5.
sampling_plan.policy: Report the original .15 worst-row gate unchanged. Do not derive new acceptance thresholds from this Q5 campaign. The added corpus is diagnostic, not a replacement passing gate.

schedule_control.interpretation: llama.cpp batching alone changes selected Q5 distributions by up to 0.100646 TV. Gufo versus one-token-microbatch llama Q5 retains up to 0.068711 TV on the three selected histories, with all three top choices equal. This residual has not been isolated to a specific operator and is not a newly declared passing execution gate.

arithmetic_contract_notes.gufo: Decoder Q5_K projections take FP32 activation inputs through LaunchGEMV -> LaunchQ8KBlockGEMV -> QuantWarpBlockDot; Q5_K uses direct dequantization/dot arithmetic.
arithmetic_contract_notes.llama_source: The pinned GPU quantized matvec implementation dispatches Q5_K to vec_dot_q5_K_q8_1 and quantizes activation inputs to Q8_1.
arithmetic_contract_notes.interpretation: Source-level arithmetic differences provide a hypothesis for residual backend drift. No layer-by-layer attribution or claim that either engine is globally more accurate was established.

focused_operator_check.name: qwen_kquant_gemv_ops_test
focused_operator_check.scope: Synthetic CPU dequant/dot controls and existing fused projection/FFN checks; not a full model arithmetic oracle.

policy_assessment: The original maximum-row TV gate still fails. Its limit and original failed record were not changed.
Both local Q4 and Q5 exceed .15 maximum TV on this sample; the cutoff does not uniquely identify a defective Q5 artifact. Existing Q4 use is not proof of passing this new fidelity policy.
Q5 has a higher worst row but fewer high-TV rows, lower average divergence and smaller sample perplexity increase. Those measures express different fidelity/quality goals.
Outlier-selected cross-engine averages and single-label likelihoods are diagnostic and must not be presented as representative corpus quality.
Future acceptance-policy calibration must be separately declared and validated on held-out workloads; do not fit limits to make this Q5 campaign pass.
next_steps: Record/reference prompt batching, activation precision and cache/storage contracts before extending same-weight engine-parity claims.

If the residual execution gap is pursued, replay the selected failing histories with operator/layer captures and an independent precision-matched dequantized-weight oracle; do not assume llama quantized outputs are exact FP32 truth.
Calibrate any future quantization acceptance policy separately, retaining tail diagnostics, held-out likelihood and capability checks and the original failed verdict.

Linux and performance were not measured.
